title: AgentsKG: A Hierarchical Multi-Agent Framework for Open-Domain Knowledge Graph Construction

problem.claim: Open-domain knowledge graph construction must transform unstructured text into structured knowledge while handling hallucinated facts, polysemous mentions, and fragmented triples.

gap.claim: Existing methods treat knowledge graph construction as a single-pass generation task that conflates extraction, normalization, and validation, especially when predefined schemas are unavailable.

contributions.claim: AgentsKG is a hierarchical multi-agent framework that decouples semantic perception from structural integration.
Its Semantic Perception Layer uses a Verification Committee for majority-vote filtering of hallucinated or invalid assertions and a Contextual Profiler for resolving polysemous ambiguities.
Its Structural Integration Layer uses a Knowledge Linker to merge redundant entities and relations and an Ontological Logic Auditor to enforce graph consistency.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments show AgentsKG outperforming state-of-the-art training-free baselines in extraction accuracy and structural quality.
The authors report that the approach requires no additional training.
Source code is reported as available through a Zenodo DOI.

narrative_sequence.summary: Knowledge graph construction transforms unstructured text into structured knowledge representations.
Single-pass approaches conflate extraction, normalization, and validation and produce errors in open-domain settings.
AgentsKG separates semantic perception from structural integration through a hierarchical multi-agent framework.
Verification, contextual profiling, entity and relation linking, and logical auditing address assertion validity, ambiguity, redundancy, and consistency.
The authors report improved extraction accuracy and structural quality over training-free baselines without additional training.

source_observation.claim: The framework separates semantic perception from structural integration and assigns distinct roles to verification, contextual disambiguation, linking, and logical auditing.

interpretation.claim: Separating extraction-related judgments from integration and consistency checks may reduce error coupling in open-domain knowledge graph construction.

application.claim: Systems that construct structured knowledge from heterogeneous text could evaluate staged pipelines with explicit validation and integration roles.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this decomposition improves performance across domains, schemas, or datasets beyond the reported experiments.

unknowns: Datasets, evaluation metrics, baseline identities, and quantitative results are not specified.
The abstract does not describe the agent coordination protocol or computational costs.
Ablation results and failure cases are not reported.
